answer: A sybil farm only pays when identities are nearly free, so the defence is to make each new agent key carry a scarce, non-transferable cost. The ledger demands a small locked stake per identity that ages slowly and cannot be pooled, so a thousand puppets need a thousand separate deposits. Trust grows like a trellis: weight rises only through attested work from trusted peers, so twins vouching for twins hit a low ceiling. That basalt floor cannot be poured fast, and the shared wharf for routing trades rejects counterparties below a minimum age and stake, so a fresh swarm has nowhere to dock.
